metadata.note: These lines are drawn to communicate that a boundary is contested, not to adjudicate it. Geometry is simplified.

properties.name: Russia–Ukraine recognised border
properties.note: The internationally recognised border. It is not the current line of control — see the line of contact layer for that.

properties.name: Transnistria administrative line
properties.note: A breakaway strip along the left bank of the Dniester, outside Chișinău's control since 1992 and host to a Russian military presence.

properties.name: Abkhazia administrative line
properties.note: Georgian territory outside Tbilisi's control since the 1990s, recognised as independent by Russia after the 2008 war.

properties.name: South Ossetia administrative line
properties.note: Georgian territory outside Tbilisi's control, recognised as independent by Russia after the 2008 war. The line has crept south in places through so-called borderisation.

properties.name: Cyprus Green Line
properties.note: The UN buffer zone dividing the island since 1974. The north is recognised only by Türkiye.

properties.name: Kosovo–Serbia boundary
properties.note: Kosovo declared independence in 2008. Serbia and several EU members do not recognise it; the northern municipalities remain the friction point.

properties.name: Armenia–Azerbaijan delimitation
properties.note: Azerbaijan regained Nagorno-Karabakh in 2023. Formal delimitation of the interstate border is still incomplete, including around the exclaves and the Syunik corridor.
